Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service — Stenvale Aria 3 recalibration

I told Dana I’d write this up after my Aria 3 had been through a real trial. It has now made it through eight days of a civil trial, so here’s my experience with Harbor Point Steno Service in Towson.

I dropped off my Stenvale Aria 3 on Monday, October 19, for a full recalibration, number bar sensor inspection, cleaning and firmware update. I picked it up Tuesday, October 27: six business days, against an estimate of ten. The quoted price was $285. The final total was $310, including a $25 battery replacement. I paid by card, personally; as with all my equipment, there was no court reimbursement. Harbor Point provided an Aria 2 loaner, which I returned at pickup.

The work held up under use. My first full day back was expert testimony from an engineer who spoke in numbers. The number bar didn’t double a single stroke. The invoice lists the recalibration, sensor replacement, cleaning, firmware update and battery replacement, and includes a 90-day warranty. The Aria also came back with a printed, one-page service sheet listing every adjustment. I’ve never had that from anyone else, and I found it useful.

Gloria asked before replacing the battery, which was holding about 60% of its rated capacity. I appreciated being asked rather than finding an extra charge on the invoice. The $310 total seems fair to me for the work done.

There are a couple of practical caveats. I called on Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress. The call rang out, and there was no voicemail box set up. Gloria emailed the following day, so I did get a response, but the phone setup is a real weakness. The line is staffed Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4. If you’re working a Monday docket and need to reach someone, plan accordingly.

The loaner’s tilt arm slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition. I propped it with a legal pad for the rest of the day and emailed Gloria about it afterward. She thanked me for the heads-up and said they would repair the arm. That made the loaner less convenient than it should have been, though it didn’t affect the repair of my own machine.

Harbor Point is a two-person shop off York Road, with free parking in back. For Dana: based on this visit, I’d trust them with your Aria 3. The work on mine held up through a demanding trial, and Gloria was careful about the additional charge. Just don’t count on reaching them by phone outside their limited hours.
